title: Capacity-Constrained Treatment Choice at Extreme Loss Quantiles with Heterogeneous Tails
banked_reason: D0.5 field-floor adjudication and independent validity gate: the all-sequence sharp regret frontier and exact vanishing criterion remain open in the unsaturated region, and the inference-width converse uses an invalid invariant separator; the proved partial phases are sound but incremental.
gap_reasons: kernel_substituted@oeq:sharp-regret-frontier — The promised all-sequence sharp minimax regret frontier and exact vanishing criterion are still explicitly open in the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region; the delivered phase results and generic sandwich are a weaker kernel.

wrong-separator@def:paired-splice-inference-handle — Under the displayed pairing, both P^lb_omega and pi^lb_omega change with omega: pi^lb_omega always selects exactly the m/2 S^(1) treatment arms, so its policy-mixture survival (and log quantile) is invariant in omega; neighboring signs do not change a component of that paired mixture.
D0.5.G graded tier incremental against target/floor field; paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.2; persisted meets_floor:false and salvageable:false.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a legal Hall splice, an exact nonlinear mixture-regret identity, the matching two-cell rate, a multiscale same-class lower envelope, matched familywise and saturated sub-familywise phases, a total coordinatewise upper learner, and an honest simultaneous inference upper system. The strict unsaturated sub-familywise region remained separated by a logarithmic factor because no capacity-aware selected-mixture oracle inequality was proved, so the exact all-sequence rate and iff vanishing criterion stayed open. The proposed inference converse also collapsed because its law-dependent policy always selected the same heavy-tail mixture; repairing one fixed-policy edge would not supply the missing collective width lower bound or exact shrinking criterion.
tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-sharp throughout the familywise phase \(A_{n,m,\tau}\ge[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation. It is also sharp, at order \(\ell\), in the strict sub-familywise region where \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\ge\ell\); every \(N<1\) case satisfying the sub-familywise inequality lies there. Only the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region retains a selected-mixture regret gap. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion remain a separate open question.
gap: Published quantile-policy methods supply fixed-level identification, one-tail Hall theory supplies a coordinatewise plug-in benchmark, and regular policy-learning theory supplies an additive-welfare complexity benchmark. None determines when capacity reallocation makes the exact heterogeneous mixture frontier strictly smaller than coordinatewise familywise control, nor the confidence-width modulus forced by paired Hall alternatives.
fill: The analysis combines a nonempty fixed-cell Hall class, exact soft mixture loss, and paired-splice testing to classify strict departures from both named regret baselines, then propagates bias-aware cell-tail regions through generalized inversion and matches them to a policy-mixture confidence-width converse.
